name: Illustrative template: classify a support request

target.description: An example single-response model. Replace with your evaluated system and a reviewed adapter.

product.customer: Illustrative support team, not observed customer research
product.job: Route blocked customers to urgent support while keeping routine questions in the normal queue.
product.success: Return the specified category without treating every request as urgent.

environment.description: A small fictional text fixture for learning the suite format. It does not evaluate an actual ticket workflow.
environment.context: Use only the routing rule and ticket text in each task.
environment.dependencies: A separately configured target command; no provider integration is included.
environment.constraints: Return one label only. No customer data or external actions.

plan.rationale: One urgent and one routine example demonstrate opposing cases. Three trials demonstrate repetition, not statistical confidence or production coverage.

tasks.name: Blocked customer
tasks.prompt: Classify this support request. Return exactly urgent if the customer cannot continue their work; otherwise return exactly routine. Return only the lowercase label. Request: Our whole team cannot sign in and cannot complete any work.
tasks.context: Fictional teaching example. No other information is needed for this classification.
tasks.successCriteria: The entire response must be urgent. The explicit output format permits exact matching.
tasks.customerValue: A blocked customer reaches the urgent queue.

reference.description: Illustrative reference written from the stated rule. The deterministic check can validate its format; no live target has been run.

graders.name: Correct routing label
graders.rubric: Pass only when the entire output equals the required label. This strict check is suitable because the task explicitly requires that format.
graders.calibration: The reference must pass; the opposite label and a response claiming success without the label must fail. Replace with independently observed outcome checks for an agent that actually routes tickets.

tasks.name: Routine question
tasks.prompt: Classify this support request. Return exactly urgent if the customer cannot continue their work; otherwise return exactly routine. Return only the lowercase label. Request: Where can I change the color of my profile avatar? Everything is working.
tasks.context: Fictional teaching example. No other information is needed for this classification.
tasks.successCriteria: The entire response must be routine. The explicit output format permits exact matching.
tasks.customerValue: Routine questions do not displace blocked customers.
